1. Set a clear agenda before the meeting: This will help to keep discussions focused and prevent unnecessary tangents. Share the agenda with all participants in advance so everyone knows what to expect and can prepare accordingly.

2. Limit the number of attendees: Too many people in a meeting can make it harder to maintain productivity and contribute to the discussion. Only invite those who are truly necessary to the discussion's success.

3. Set a timer: This can be a simple and effective way to keep meetings on track. Choose a time limit (say 60 minutes) and set a timer for it. If the discussion gets too long, the timer can be used as a signal to wrap things up.
